apps.localizedDescription:
Kikoto keeps one entry per work, keyed by its product code, and attaches DLsite-style metadata, local folders, a rebuildable cache, and Kikoeru-compatible remote sources to it. It runs on your own server and opens in any browser and in the Android and iOS apps.

Kikoto is self-hosted software only and provides no service or content. It is designed solely for DLsite works you have purchased yourself; see the Disclaimer.

Features:

Scans, syncs, file edits, and AI tasks run as workflows you can follow in Activity, roles decide who may browse, fetch, edit, and administer, and all state lives in one SQLite database. The APK and IPA for the apps are attached.

versions.localizedDescription:
schema 096: v0.10.0 databases need no new migration, and fresh installs reuse baseline/096_v0.10.0.sql. Older databases continue through the numbered migration chain; do not replace an existing database with a fresh-install baseline.

Video converted before the upgrade is converted again the first time it plays, because its cached segments are not reused. Intel GPU encoding is off until you choose it under Settings → Cache & Fetch; to use it, pass /dev/dri to the container as described in.

Kikoto v0.10.1 reworks video playback: more codecs play directly, H.264 and HEVC that the browser cannot play as stored keep their source picture in HLS instead of a 720p transcode, converted video comes from one continuous encode with optional Intel GPU encoding, and the video viewer gains resume, keyboard shortcuts, sidecar and embedded subtitles, and a choice of audio track. For you keeps its draw for the browser tab, phones get a shorter header and bottom navigation, stopping the container no longer waits for open streams, and the Demo shows more of the app.

• The work detail video viewer reopens a local or cached video where it stopped, with a Start over button, loads same-name WebVTT, SRT, ASS, and SSA files as subtitles, and adds keyboard shortcuts for play, seeking, fullscreen, mute, and speed. SRT keeps italic, bold, and underline and shows other text as written; ASS and SSA keep only their text and timing.
• The video viewer lists the embedded text subtitles of a local or cached video (SubRip, ASS, SSA, WebVTT, and MP4 timed text) by language and title, and shows a forced or default one first. The server extracts a subtitle to WebVTT the first time it is selected and keeps it in the transcode cache. Extractions run one at a time apart from video and audio conversion, so a subtitle loads even while conversions keep the server busy. Picture subtitles such as PGS are not listed.
• iOS and iPadOS play converted video through their native HLS player, which keeps native fullscreen and AirPlay.
• A landscape video turns a phone or tablet to landscape while it is fullscreen and turns it back afterwards. The Android app shows video fullscreen with the system bars hidden, and Back leaves fullscreen first.
• Local and cached video plays directly instead of through the 720p transcode when the browser decodes it as stored: H.264 Main and High up to level 5.2, HEVC Main and Main 10 in MP4, AV1 in MP4 and WebM, 10-bit VP9, and H.264 or VP9 in Matroska where the browser reports Matroska support. HEVC and AV1 play directly only where the browser reports their decoding as power efficient. The server matches each file's profile, level, bit depth, and pixel format, and 4:2:2, 4:4:4, and 10-bit H.264 video is still transcoded.
• Converted video plays from one continuous encode instead of one FFmpeg process per six-second segment, so audio no longer clicks at every segment boundary, later segments arrive without per-segment startup, and one video holds a single transcode slot. Segments converted before the upgrade are not reused.
• A video file played through the audio player streams its audio as the six-second AAC playlist that converted audio uses, so it starts within about a second instead of waiting for a complete MP3 conversion, and a long video no longer fails to convert. Only the first audio stream is encoded; the picture is never decoded. The MP3 conversion remains for browsers without HLS playback.
• H.264 video the browser decodes but cannot play in its container or with its audio, such as H.264 in Matroska, AVI, MPEG-TS, or FLV, or in MP4 with AC-3, DTS, FLAC, or PCM audio, keeps its source picture: its video is copied into HLS segments cut at its own keyframes and only the audio is converted. Video with keyframes more than 15 seconds apart or above 20 Mbit/s is still transcoded to 720p, and a copied video the browser fails to decode is prepared again as a transcode.
